newsitem.title: USA: Brazil Makro launches Level One ADR.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Makro launches Level One ADR.

text.p: Brazilian cash-and-carry wholesaler Makro Atacadista SA said on Monday it had launched a Level One American Depositary Receipt (ADR) program.
The company said in a statement that Makro's ADRs were trading over the counter on the National Association of Securities Dealers' Bulletin Board. Its symbol is MKRAY and each ADR equals 10 shares.
Citibank is Makro's depositary institution. Makro is a unit of the Netherlands' SHV Makro.
A Level One ADR enables conversion of existing shares publicly traded in the home market into dollar-denominated ADRs.
Unlike Level Two or Three ADRs, Level Ones do not require filing of a Securities and Exchange Commission registration statement and annual report for foreign private issuers.
Makro also has so-called Rule 144A ADRs, privately placed securities traded by qualified institutional buyers.
